To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the affinity of a group of data in a program can be measured by the distance between the group and its nearest neighbor and that the nearest neighbor of each group can be found by k-distance analysis, which is a fast and simple algorithm that can be implemented as a preprocessor.

(i) the affinity of program data can be measured using the k-distance metric; (ii) k-distance analysis is an efficient, effective, and robust method for array regrouped; and (iii) k-distance analysis can be used to split structures to improve cache locality.
the reference affinity of program data can be measured by k-distance and that k-distance is a powerful heuristic for array regrouped and structure splitting.

, while programmers and compilers can do a reasonable job in partitioning data, they can do a much better job if they use the whole-program reference trace as a guide.

a whole-program reference trace is a good source of information for the data layout of a program.
